title: HIV latent reservoir and a sterilizing cure
bottleneck: Antiretroviral therapy suppresses HIV but cannot touch latent proviruses integrated into resting CD4+ T cells, which reignite infection if treatment stops. Current latency-reversing agents have shown limited efficacy in shrinking the reservoir in clinical studies, and the persistence of latent virus is described as the greatest barrier to curing AIDS.
why_it_blocks: Over 40 million people live with HIV; lifelong therapy is a triumph but also a burden, and a cure requires eliminating a reservoir that is invisible to drugs and the immune system.
current_state: Novel approaches, including virus-like-particle latency reversers far more potent than existing agents, BRD9 inhibitors, and CARD8-inflammasome kill strategies, show preclinical and early clinical promise. No strategy has yet produced a sterilizing cure.
